events.title: The death of Rabanus Maurus
events.shortBlurb: The great teacher-monk of the Carolingian age, archbishop of Mainz, died leaving Germany a legacy of learning and the hymn Veni Creator…
body: On 4 February 856 died Rabanus Maurus at Winkel on the Rhine, abbot of Fulda and archbishop of Mainz, the foremost teacher of the Carolingian age. Born of noble parents at Mainz about 780, he became a monk of Fulda and studied under Alcuin at Tours, who named him Maurus after the beloved disciple of St. Benedict.

Placed over the abbey school of Fulda in 803 and abbot from 822, he made Fulda the greatest center of learning north of the Alps; his pupils included Walafrid Strabo, Lupus of Ferrières, and Otfrid of Weissenburg. His writings embraced commentaries on nearly the whole of Scripture, a treatise on the formation of clergy, and an encyclopedia in twenty-two books, earning him the title Praeceptor Germaniae, the teacher of Germany.

Resigning his abbey in 842 for prayer and study, he was called in 847 to the see of Mainz, where he won the love of his people by his charity in a time of famine. He is traditionally held the author of the hymn to the Holy Spirit, Veni Creator Spiritus, still sung at Pentecost, ordinations, and the opening of conclaves.
